name: TerraPower
short_description: Bill Gates-backed developer of sodium fast reactors and the Natrium SMR.
why_relevant: First advanced-reactor construction start permitted in the US in decades.
history: Founded in 2006 with backing from Bill Gates, TerraPower evolved from early traveling-wave reactor studies into the Natrium platform, pairing a sodium-cooled fast reactor with molten-salt storage. After years of licensing and design work, it delivered major licensing and funding milestones and in 2024 broke ground at Kemmerer, Wyoming, on its first Natrium demonstration plant, the first advanced-reactor construction start permitted in the US in decades. The company is now scaling its supply chain and targeting commercial Natrium deployments in the 2030s.

name: Commonwealth Fusion Systems
short_description: Spinout of MIT using high-temperature superconducting magnets for SPARC.
why_relevant: The fusion company that says power on the grid before 2035.
history: Spun out of MIT in 2018, Commonwealth Fusion Systems set out to accelerate fusion commercialization with high-temperature superconducting magnets. It raised landmark funding rounds in 2021 led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Tiger Global, then demonstrated its world-record HTS magnet, de-risking the SPARC design. The company is now building SPARC at its Devens, Massachusetts facility and aims to deliver net-energy fusion experiments by the mid-2020s, with plans for the ARC grid power plant before 2035.

name: Helion Energy
short_description: Pulsed, fuel-mixture fusion approach already selling first electricity agreements.
why_relevant: Signed a world-first fusion electricity purchase agreement.
history: Founded in 2013 by David Kirtley, Helion Energy developed a pulsed, non-cryogenic fusion approach using a deuterium-helium-3 fuel mix. The company reached repeated high-temperature plasma milestones and in 2021 raised one of the largest fusion funding rounds, backed by Sam Altman and others. In 2023 it signed a world-first fusion power purchase agreement with Microsoft, and it is now building its Polaris prototype, targeting net-electricity demonstration by 2027 and commercial plants by the early 2030s.

name: TAE Technologies
short_description: The longest-running private fusion company, now building Copernicus.
why_relevant: Decades of deuterium-boron approach for aneutronic power.
history: Founded in 1998, TAE Technologies is the longest-running private fusion company, originally spun out of University of California plasma physics research. It spent two decades maturing a beam-driven field-reversed configuration aimed at aneutronic deuterium-boron fuel, passing a series of scaled experiments including its Norman device. With backing from investors such as Google, it is now constructing Copernicus, designed to demonstrate net energy, and continues working toward clean fusion power plants that avoid radioactive waste.

name: General Fusion
short_description: Canada's leading magnetized-target approach to commercial fusion.
why_relevant: Institution-scale asset that British Columbia has scoped into a demo plant.
history: Founded in 2002 by scientists including Michel Laberge, General Fusion pioneered magnetized target fusion, compressing magnetized plasmas with mechanical pistons. It grew with Canadian institutional support and in 2021 received a funding commitment from the Government of Canada for a machine to achieve scientific breakeven. The company partnered with the UK Atomic Energy Authority on a Fusion Demonstration Plant and continues advancing engineering, with British Columbia scoping a commercial-scale demonstration plant in the region.

name: Radiant Nuclear
short_description: Develops kilo-watt scale modular nuclear reactors for remote microgrids.
why_relevant: Turnkey hot swap truck-mounted reactors for power in a crate.
history: Founded in 2019, Radiant Nuclear develops Kaleidos, a truck-transportable microreactor delivering kilowatt- to megawatt-scale power for remote microgrids and industrial sites. The company raised early venture rounds and won US Department of Defense contracts, advancing its turnkey hot-swap reactor design through detailed engineering and safety review. Radiant is now progressing toward a first criticality demonstration this decade, positioning itself to offer grid-independent power in a crate for off-grid and emergency applications.

name: NuScale Power
short_description: First SMR design to receive US NRC certification.
why_relevant: Certified SMR design comparing economics down under 100 MW.
history: Founded in 2007, NuScale Power developed the first small modular reactor design to receive US Nuclear Regulatory Commission certification, a milestone reached in 2023. It grew out of Oregon State University research and became a publicly traded company in 2022, leading the now-canceled Carbon Free Power Project in Idaho while pursuing new customers. NuScale continues marketing its 77 MWe VOYGR plants internationally, from Romania to Poland, targeting first deployments later this decade.

name: Oklo
short_description: First fast-spectrum microreactor with commercial permits to build.
why_relevant: Deploy-anywhere 15 MW plants with 20-year fuel life.
history: Founded in 2013 by Jacob DeWitte and Caroline Cochran, Oklo developed the Aurora fast-spectrum microreactor, a 15 MW plant with 20-year fuel life powered by recycled fuel. The company went public in 2024 and became the first in the US to secure a site-use permit and commercial license application milestones for an advanced microreactor. Oklo has since signed power purchase agreements with data-center and industrial customers, signaling momentum toward first deployments in the late 2020s.

name: Kairos Power
short_description: Fluoride-salt-cooled high-temperature reactor with rapid prototyping ethos.
why_relevant: Iterative prototyping fixed expensive first-of-a-kind surprises.
history: Founded in 2016 by Mike Laufer and Per Peterson, Kairos Power developed the Hermes fluoride-salt-cooled high-temperature reactor using a rapid iterative prototyping philosophy. It became the first advanced non-light-water reactor to receive a construction permit from the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, approved in 2025 for its Hermes demonstration at Oak Ridge, Tennessee. With a Department of Energy deployment award and partnerships with Google and Southern Company, Kairos plans to demonstrate the technology this decade and scale to commercial KFHR plants.

name: Oxford PV
short_description: Perovskite-on-silicon tandem solar cells that beat the single-junction limit.
why_relevant: Pushed commercial solar efficiency past the old 30 percent ceiling.
history: Founded in 2010 as a spinout of the University of Oxford, Oxford PV pioneered perovskite-on-silicon tandem solar cells that exceed the traditional single-junction efficiency limit. The company raised venture funding, opened manufacturing in Germany, and in 2018 set a world record with a 28 percent efficient perovskite-silicon cell. It has since shipped early commercial tandem modules and announced a giga-scale production partnership, positioning itself to bring the technology to the mass solar market in the coming years.

name: Carbon Engineering
short_description: Pioneer of industrial direct air capture of CO2 for 1PointFive conversion.
why_relevant: The DAC blueprint now copied by a dozen carbon-removal startups.
history: Founded in 2009 by David Keith, Carbon Engineering pioneered industrial direct air capture of CO2 and an air-to-fuels pathway. It operated a demonstration plant in Squamish, British Columbia, and licensed its technology to Occidental's 1PointFive subsidiary, which broke ground on the first large-scale DAC plant in Texas in 2022. The company became part of the Occidental umbrella in 2023 and continues scaling its technology as the reference DAC blueprint for a growing carbon-removal industry.

name: Climeworks
short_description: Operates the largest commercial direct air capture plant, Mammoth.
why_relevant: Sells permanent removal at ton-scale to major corporations.
history: Founded in 2009 as an ETH Zurich spinout, Climeworks commercialized modular direct air capture using reusable filter technology. It launched Orca in Iceland in 2021, the world's first commercial DAC plant, and doubled down with Mammoth, which began operations in 2024 at roughly ten times larger capacity. Backed by major investors and government programs, Climeworks sells permanent carbon removal credits to corporations such as Microsoft, Stripe, and Airbus, while expanding projects across Europe, Iceland, and Kenya.

name: Heirloom Carbon
short_description: Accelerates natural limestone-mineral CO2 uptake into days.
why_relevant: Uses carbonate ovens to turn neglected minerals into removal credit mills.
history: Founded in 2020 by Shashank Samala, Heirloom Carbon accelerates the natural CO2 absorption of limestone, shrinking a multi-year mineralization process to days using renewable-powered electric kilns. It raised prominent early funding, won a Department of Energy grant, and opened its first commercial facility in Tracy, California, in late 2023. Heirloom has signed carbon removal offtake agreements with Microsoft, Klarna, and others, and is scaling toward facilities that can remove megatons of CO2 cost-effectively.

name: Redwood Materials
short_description: Turns end-of-life EV batteries back into cathode and anode materials.
why_relevant: Supply-chain gold from recycling could cover a third of American battery need.
history: Founded in 2017 by Tesla co-founder J.B. Straubel, Redwood Materials built a closed-loop battery recycling pipeline for end-of-life EV packs and manufacturing scrap. The company raised over $1 billion from investors and the Department of Energy, and opened facilities in Nevada for recycling and in South Carolina for cathode and anode production. Redwood has signed supply agreements with major automakers and battery partners, working toward recycling enough material to supply a meaningful share of American battery demand.

name: Ascend Elements
short_description: Hydro-to-cathode process recycles battery waste into usable cathode powder.
why_relevant: First US gigafactory-scale cathode production from spent cells.
history: Founded in 2015, Ascend Elements developed a patented hydro-to-cathode process that recycles battery manufacturing waste and end-of-life cells into usable cathode powder. Based in Massachusetts, the company won a Department of Energy investment and completed a commercial-scale battery recycling facility in Georgia in 2023. It is now building what would be the first US gigafactory-scale cathode plant from recycled material in Kentucky, with offtake agreements with major battery and automotive players.

name: Li-Cycle
short_description: Spoke-and-hub lithium-ion recycling network with patented submerged shredding.
why_relevant: No-smelting recycling that recovers 95 percent of critical battery mass.
history: Founded in 2016, Li-Cycle built a spoke-and-hub lithium-ion recycling network using patented submerged shredding that recovers up to 95 percent of battery materials without smelting. The Toronto-based company scaled collection spokes across North America and Europe and listed on the New York Stock Exchange in 2021. After pausing construction on its Rochester, New York hub amid cost overruns, Li-Cycle secured strategic financing from Glencore and revised its hub strategy to refocus on commercial operations.

name: Electric Hydrogen
short_description: Builds gigawatt-scale, low-cost electrolyzers for green hydrogen.
why_relevant: Aims to make hydrogen cost-competitive with fossil across heavy industry.
history: Founded in 2021 by veterans of First Solar and Tesla, Electric Hydrogen developed gigawatt-scale, low-cost electrolyzer stacks for green hydrogen production. It raised significant funding, including a $380 million Series C round in 2023 led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures and others, one of the largest for an electrolyzer maker. The company opened a factory in Natick, Massachusetts, and signed early supply agreements, targeting plants that make hydrogen competitive with fossil feedstocks in heavy industry.

name: Ohmium
short_description: Modular PEM electrolyzers shipped worldwide for renewable hydrogen.
why_relevant: Containerized electrolyzers turn any grid corner into a clean hydrogen hub.
history: Founded in 2020, Ohmium designs modular, containerized PEM electrolyzers that can be deployed anywhere renewable power is available. The company established manufacturing in India and the United States and grew an order pipeline of several gigawatts across Asia, Europe, and North America, backed by investors such as Energy Impact Partners. Ohmium's plug-and-play electrolyzer stacks let customers commission hydrogen capacity in days, positioning the company for a leading role in the distributed green hydrogen market.

name: Sublime Systems
short_description: Makes cement with an electrochemical process instead of kilns.
why_relevant: Helps demolish the 8-percent-of-CO2 problem hidden inside concrete.
history: Founded in 2020 as a spinout of MIT, Sublime Systems developed an electrochemical process that makes low-carbon cement at ambient temperature instead of superheating kilns. The company raised over $100 million from investors such as Lowercarbon Capital, won a Department of Energy award, and partnered with Holcim as it scales. Having validated the chemistry in pilots, Sublime is building its first commercial production facility, targeting the roughly 8 percent of global CO2 emissions that cement manufacturing contributes.

name: Brimstone Energy
short_description: Produces cement from silicate rocks without releasing process CO2.
why_relevant: Sells a carbonate-negative Portland-cement-equivalent replacement.
history: Founded in 2019 by Cody Finke, Brimstone Energy developed a chemical process that makes Portland cement from silicate rocks instead of limestone, eliminating the process CO2 emissions that dominate cement's footprint. The Oakland, California startup raised over $80 million, including from Bill Gates's Breakthrough Energy Ventures, and became the first decarbonized-cement company to secure Department of Energy backing. Brimstone is scaling a pilot plant that could deliver carbon-negative cement at traditional Portland quality and cost.

name: Boston Metal
short_description: Molten oxide electrolysis makes steel without blast furnaces or carbon.
why_relevant: A path to near-zero-carbon steel without scaling hydrogen plants first.
history: Founded in 2012 as an MIT spinout, Boston Metal developed molten oxide electrolysis to produce steel, iron, and metals from any ore feedstock without blast furnaces or carbon. The company raised over $300 million, including from Breakthrough Energy Ventures and ArcelorMittal, and opened a commercial plant in Brazil producing high-value metals like tin and niobium. It is now scaling gigawatt-class MOE cells to make green steel at competitive cost for the global steel market.

name: Electra
short_description: Electro-refines steel at low temperatures, cutting its energy needs.
why_relevant: Powered refining opens steelmaking to intermittent renewables.
history: Founded in 2020, Electra developed a low-temperature electrochemical refining process that makes iron and steel directly from ore while using 60-70 percent less energy than conventional routes. The Boulder, Colorado company raised funding from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, and others, and won a Department of Defense supply-chain contract. Electra is commercializing its 30-ton-per-day pilot plant and aims to make near-zero-carbon steel that can run on intermittent renewable power.

name: Rondo Energy
short_description: Bricks-based heat storage that dispatches industrial process heat.
why_relevant: Industrial heat being electrified with cheap minerals, not rare materials.
history: Founded in 2020, Rondo Energy developed a heat battery made of ordinary refractory brick that converts renewable electricity into high-temperature industrial heat on demand. Backed by Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, and others, the company deployed its first installation in Thailand and announced expansion projects across Europe and the US. Rondo's low-cost thermal storage lets factories replace fossil-fueled boilers by time-shifting cheap wind and solar power into steam and process heat.

name: Antora Energy
short_description: Carbon-block thermal batteries discharging heat and power on demand.
why_relevant: Bridges the grid with stored heat that converts to dispatchable electricity.
history: Founded in 2018 by Stanford alumni, Antora Energy built carbon-block thermal batteries that store electricity as heat and return it as both process heat and dispatchable power via thermophotovoltaic conversion. The company raised significant funding, including a $150 million round in 2023, and signed partnership deals with utilities and industrial operators. Antora is commissioning modular systems that convert stored heat into flexible electricity, helping grid operators integrate more intermittent renewable generation.

name: Monolith
short_description: Methane pyrolysis splits natural gas into hydrogen and solid carbon black.
why_relevant: Commodity hydrogen without CO2 and a carbon black co-product.
history: Founded in 2020, Monolith developed methane pyrolysis, a process that splits natural gas into clean hydrogen and solid carbon black instead of emitting CO2. The Nebraska-based company secured a $1 billion Department of Energy loan and expanded its Olive Creek plant, one of the world's largest clean hydrogen facilities, with investment from SK and Mitsubishi. Monolith is scaling to supply low-cost hydrogen for ammonia, refining, and fuel-cell uses, while selling carbon black co-product to tire and plastics customers.

name: Stegra (H2 Green Steel)
short_description: Building a large green hydrogen steel plant in northern Sweden.
why_relevant: Flagship commercial proof that hydrogen steel can be delivered at scale.
history: Founded in 2020 as H2 Green Steel and rebranded Stegra in 2024, the company is building one of the world's first large-scale green hydrogen steel plants in Boden, northern Sweden. It assembled a 6.5 billion euro financing package, one of the largest for a European industrial startup, and raised additional equity from investors including Al Gore's Generation Investment Management. Stegra aims to start delivering hydrogen-reduced steel to automakers and industry from 2026, marking a flagship commercial proof for hydrogen steel at scale.

name: Twelve
short_description: Electrochemistry turns CO2 into jet fuel, plastics and critical chemicals.
why_relevant: E-Jet fuel from captured CO2 lectured as a practical SAF supply answer.
history: Founded in 2015, Twelve uses electrochemistry to transform captured CO2 into jet fuel, plastics, and critical chemicals. The Berkeley, California company raised over $200 million, including Microsoft's Climate Innovation Fund, and achieved a 100-fold scale-up of its electrolyzer technology. Twelve launched its E-Jet fuel in the US and won contracts with airlines and the Air Force, while also producing polypropylene and other feedstocks, and is now building a larger commercial plant.

name: Air Company
short_description: Converts CO2 and water into sustainable aviation fuel and spirits.
why_relevant: Closed-loop fuel and vodka from thin air that customers actually buy.
history: Founded in 2017, Air Company developed a proprietary process that converts CO2 and water into sustainable aviation fuel, spirits, and fragrance ingredients using renewable energy. The New York-based startup partnered to supply its Airmade SAF and made early commercial sales, treating its vodka product as proof of the carbon-zero cycle. Backed by investors including Toyota Ventures, Air Company is scaling toward industrial fuel production and expanding its aviation customer pipeline.

name: Amogy
short_description: Turns ammonia into electric power for trucks, ships and heavy equipment.
why_relevant: Green ammonia as liquid hydrogen for transport, without cryogenics.
history: Founded in 2020 as an MIT spinout, Amogy developed a system that cracks green ammonia into hydrogen and runs it through fuel cells to produce electric power for trucks, ships, and heavy equipment. The Brooklyn-based company passed world-first ammonia-powered demonstrations, including a tractor in 2022, a semi-truck in 2023, and a tugboat later that year. Amogy raised over $200 million, including from Amazon's Climate Pledge Fund, and is now adapting its system for larger marine vessels.

name: ZeroAvia
short_description: Develops hydrogen-electric powertrains for zero-emission regional flight.
why_relevant: World-first fuel-cell commercial aircraft flight at 19-passenger scale.
history: Founded in 2017 by Val Miftakhov, ZeroAvia develops hydrogen-electric powertrains for regional aviation using fuel cells and electric motors. It achieved the world's first fuel-cell commercial aircraft flight with a six-seat Piper in 2020 and followed with a 19-seat aircraft prototype in 2023, targeting entry into service this decade. The UK-US company has raised over $300 million from investors including United Airlines and is certifying its ZA600 powertrain for regional aircraft and converted turboprops.

name: Sunfire
short_description: EU leader in pressurized alkaline and solid-oxide electrolysis.
why_relevant: Efficiency-leading solid-oxide electrolyzers for industrial e-refineries.
history: Founded in 2010, Sunfire became a European leader in pressurized alkaline and solid-oxide electrolysis for green hydrogen and e-fuels. The Dresden-based company raised serial funding from investors like Planet A, secured EU and national project support, and won orders for industrial-scale plants including Norsk e-Fuel in Norway. Sunfire now offers both efficiency-leading SOEC and robust alkaline platforms, positioning itself to supply the e-refineries and chemical plants decarbonizing across Europe.

name: Verkor
short_description: Building France's battery cell plants for EV artificial intelligence dashboards.
why_relevant: Europe's answer to keeping cell production inside its own supply chain.
history: Founded in 2019, Verkor is building France's flagship battery gigafactories to supply cells for electric vehicles and industrial applications. The Grenoble-based company raised over 2 billion euros in financing, anchored by Renault and mining giant Macquarie, and broke ground on its Dunkirk gigafactory in 2023. Verkor plans to ramp production to 16 GWh initially and 50 GWh by 2030, strengthening Europe's capacity to make critical cells within its own supply chain.
